title: Please consider non dismissible notifications
body:
Feature Request: Add Persistent, Action-Based Notifications for Reminders (ADHD Use Case)

⸻

Message:

Dear Apple Team,

I’m writing to request a feature enhancement for the Apple Reminders app that would be incredibly helpful to users like me who live with ADHD and face daily challenges with memory, time-blindness, and task initiation.

⸻

🔔 Feature Request: Persistent, Non-Dismissible Notifications for Reminders

⸻

What I’m Requesting:
	1.	Persistent Lock Screen / Banner Notification
	•	The reminder stays permanently visible on the lock screen and in the notification center.
	•	It cannot be swiped away or dismissed until the task is either:
	•	Marked as completed, or
	•	Deleted manually within the Reminders app.
	2.	Customizable Repeating Alerts
	•	Users can define a frequency (e.g., every 15, 30, or 60 minutes) to repeat a sound, vibration, or notification until the task is completed.
	3.	A Toggle for “Persistent” or “Nag Mode”
	•	A simple switch when creating a reminder to turn on this persistent mode — ideally alongside existing options like time, priority, and location.

⸻

Why It Matters (ADHD Use Case):

As someone with ADHD, it’s easy to miss or accidentally dismiss notifications. Once they disappear, the task is often completely forgotten.
Gentle or one-time reminders are simply not effective for users like me.

This feature would act as a strong external cue — something that remains in front of me until I complete the task. It would greatly support my productivity, independence, and mental clarity.

⸻

I believe this would also benefit many users beyond ADHD — including those managing caregiving tasks, medication schedules, or urgent work obligations.

Thank you for continuing to create thoughtful, accessible tools. I hope this idea can be considered for a future iOS update.
